Open World v2.48 — the real Earth at 1:1 in the Capital Rift look: real lake outlines (10 m source data) so every great lake has its true shape — solid clean blue water shore to shore with green pastures meeting the waterline (the lake plane rides 80 cm clear of the land, past the reach of depth noise at any altitude), zero fog anywhere, free camera roam with no distance cap from your tycoon, and a zoom that now climbs from street level all the way to a 23,000 km whole-world view, neighborhoods of houses around every city (ring roads and tree-named lanes of lawns, driveways and pitched roofs out to ~2.4 km, every house clickable), woodland belts around the cities beyond the last yard, real 3D forest across every other dry-land chunk of the open country (never in the cities, never in water), open-house interiors — click any building to open it like a dollhouse, then pick a floor (big buildings) or a named room (houses and small shops) from the inspector panel (every other building keeps its full silhouette), every one of those rooms and floors for sale or for rent (buy it outright — yours forever, tenants pay you daily — or rent it with a two-day deposit; your holdings glow gold and pay you every day), a patchwork of buyable farm parcels over every mile of open country around the cities (rectangles of all shapes and sizes in every shade of green like a satellite view — hover one for its price, click to buy it, and the tenant farmers pay you daily — at premium prices since v2.46: about ten times the cost for about three times the rent), landlord rentals at your own price (list any plot, office suite, room, floor or farm parcel you own and tenants pay your daily rate — price it above the local market and it may sit empty while the market looks), and machines you install inside the rooms and floors you own (six kinds from a vending machine to a server rack — click a spot in your own space to set each one down, and every machine pays you every day), mining claims you stake yourself in the open country (select any rectangle of land past the suburbs, set your machinery on its ring and dig — the ore sells daily and the pit terraces deeper until it’s worked out), and the same streets, buildings, plots and roads on dry land only
